m.d: If a person offs someone, they kill him or her.
m.e: I heard they offed Jimmy by drowning.

m.d: If food is off, it is not good to eat anymore.
m.e: The meat smells off.

m.d: Away from somewhere or some time.
m.e: I got ready and by 7:00 I was off to school.

m.d: If something is off it is not on.
m.e: He pushed the book off the table, and it fell to the floor.

m.d: Out of a vehicle such as a train, bus, etc.
m.e: As the train stopped, he jumped off and ran to her.

m.d: If you're off something, you don't like or want something you wanted before.
m.e: That article really put me off meat.

m.d: If you're off some medicine, you are not using it any more.
m.e: He's been off the pain killers for a few weeks.

m.d: An office is a room or building where people sit at desks and work.
m.e: Her office is in the third door on the left side of the hall.

m.d: A position held by public election is an office.
m.e: They both decided to run for office.

m.d: An officer is a person in an army who has much authority. A general and a captain are two types of officers.
m.e: A soldier must obey his commanding officer.

m.d: An officer is a policeman, often called a "police officer." (Note, "officer" is often better than "policeman" because the officer could be a woman or a man.)
m.e: Officer, can you help me, I've been robbed.

m.d: An officer is someone who holds office (meaning, has authority).
m.e: The judge is an important officer of the court.

m.d: An offer is when you say you will do something or give something.
m.e: He wanted to buy my car, so he made me an offer of $5000.

m.d: If I offer something to you, that means I will give it to you if you want.
If I offer to do something for you, that means I will do it for you if you want.
When something happens often, that means that it happens many times and frequently.
m.e: I drink a lot of water and need to urinate often.

m.d: An official is a person who has certain authority.
m.e: That government official collects taxes.

m.d: Something that is official is approved by some authority.
m.e: The letter was an official document from the president.

m.d: An act of offering.
Something that has been offered; a sacrifice.
A contribution given at a religious service.
If something is done officially, it is done in an official way.
m.e: He is now officially the president.

m.d: An offense is an action that breaks the law.
m.e: Murder is a serious criminal offense.

m.d: When you give offense to someone, you do something that they don't like.
m.e: I didn't mean to give offense, but I didn't know that you don't do that in China.

m.d: The offense is the person or team who is attacking.
m.e: For the first time in the game, Arsenal goes on the offense.

m.d: An attack.
m.e: The Marines today launched a major offensive.

m.d: In a position of attacking or being able to attack.
m.e: He took the offensive in the press, accusing his opponent of corruption.

m.d: Something offensive is mean, insulting, and unpleasant.
m.e: He said something so offensive to her that she cried.

m.d: If something is offensive, it has to do with a play where the team is trying to score.
m.e: The offensive coordinator is responsible for ordering all rushing plays.

m.d: An offence is an action that breaks the law.
m.e: Murder is a serious criminal offence.

m.d: When you give offence to someone, you do something that they don't like.
m.e: I didn't mean to give offence, but I didn't know that you don't do that in China.

m.d: The offence is the person or team who is attacking.
m.e: For the first time in the game, Arsenal goes on the offence.

m.d: An act when someone makes another person unhappy. To offend someone is to make them feel disgust.
m.e: Don't offend him. It's not nice. He may fight back.

m.d: An offender is someone or something that does something wrong, usually someone who breaks the law.
m.e: The boy who took the car is a young offender, so we can't use his real name.

m.d: An offspring is either the sons, daughters, or immediate descendants of a human, animal or plant.
m.e: That lioness just gave birth to two offspring!

m.d: In the sea, away from the shore.
m.e: The men worked on an offshore oil rig.

m.d: If an activity is off-limits, someone is not allowed to do it.
If something is off-limits, someone is not allowed to access or use it.
If a place or an area is off-limits, someone is not allowed to enter or access that place or area.
If a system is offline, it is not connected (generally electronically) to a larger network.
If a machine is offline, it is not powered on.
m.e: The printer is offline for a few minutes while it starts up.

m.d: While offline.
Oft is an archaic or literary form of often.
